title: preview-verify can never reach verified=true with a live browser tab: it re-navs, then checks whether the iframe loaded since its own nav
description:
`preview-verify` appears unable to return `verified=true` whenever a browser tab is actually connected, because it issues its own `preview-nav` and then immediately asks whether the iframe has loaded SINCE that nav. The browser's load report cannot arrive before the check returns, so `lastIframeLoadedAtMs` is always less than `lastPreviewNavAtMs` and the result is `verified=false stale=true staleState=tab_connected_but_not_reloaded`.

Evidence, two consecutive `editor preview` runs on an otherwise idle session:

  run 1: iframeLoadedAt=1786879269418  navAt=1786879290491   (load 21s BEFORE the nav)
  run 2: iframeLoadedAt=1786879293331  navAt=1786879293878   (load 0.5s BEFORE the nav)

The load timestamp ADVANCES between runs (269418 -> 293331), which proves the iframe is genuinely reloading and the tab is healthy. What changes is that each invocation stamps a new `navAt`, so the freshly-arrived load is immediately older than the new nav. The comparison can never come out the other way.

Things that do NOT fix it, all tried:
- Re-issuing `preview-nav` before `preview-verify` (three times).
- Asking the USER to do a full reload of the editor browser tab, which is what the advisory text instructs. They did; `staleState` was unchanged. This is the part worth fixing first — the advisory sends the user to perform a manual step that cannot work, which reads as the tool blaming the operator for its own race.
- Interposing an ~8s settle (a full `verify-build`) between `preview-nav` and `preview-verify`. Still fails, because `preview-verify` re-navs with a fresh `_cb` before checking, discarding the settle.

Downstream impact: `demo-attest` hard-refuses with "no verified Demo capture exists for this feature yet", so the Prepare Demo step cannot be completed the intended way. The step text calls this state "a recoverable condition, not a structural reason for demo-skip", but on the evidence it is not recoverable by any action available to the agent or the user, so `demo-skip` is the only exit — which is exactly the silent-quality-loss the gate exists to prevent. A run with NO tab connected reports `no_tab_connected` and is likewise `verified=false`, so neither branch reaches green here.

Suggested fix, roughly in order: (a) have `preview-verify` wait for the iframe's load event for the nav it just issued (bounded), rather than sampling a timestamp written asynchronously; (b) failing that, compare against the nav that PRECEDED this invocation, not the one it just made; (c) at minimum, stop instructing the user to reload for `tab_connected_but_not_reloaded` when the immediately-preceding nav was self-issued — the advisory currently prescribes a remedy that cannot change the outcome.

The capture itself was never the problem: `.codeyam/preview-capture.png` rendered `/` correctly throughout, and full-page renders confirmed the change. Only the freshness ASSERTION is broken.

Observed on the puzzle-school-rebuild branch (Astro static site, cloud VM, fleet-hosted editor) while demoing the full-bleed layout feature.
